WORKSHEET · CLASS 26 · AGES 4 YEARS

Chameleon’s Color Magic Worksheet for Age 4

A chameleon waiting for its colors: pick from your key and paint each part — it changes color either way.

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

On screen the chameleon changes color with a tap; on paper your child is the magic. Choosing colors for each body part and naming them out loud turns one coloring sheet into a dozen color-word rehearsals.

  • Naming colors while using them
  • Making deliberate color choices
  • Coloring inside clear regions
  • Describing choices (“why purple?”)

On the sheet: Color the chameleon with your color key — every part a different color if you like.

WHERE THIS FITS

The class behind it.

This worksheet belongs to Colors, Mixing & Creativity (Class 26) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole colors collection lives at /worksheets/colors/. One finished sheet is a full session — download it, print it, and let the fridge door be the gallery.

Rainbow Paint Laboratory Worksheet for Age 4

Three true paint recipes to solve and color: red + yellow makes… you finish the experiment.

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The laboratory’s recipes are real paint science, and the sheet makes your child predict before coloring: guess the mixture, color the surprise circle, write the color word. Prediction is the scientific habit — sneaked in with crayons.

  • Predicting a color mixture
  • Knowing red+yellow, yellow+blue, blue+red
  • Writing color words (with help)
  • Testing predictions with real paint

On the sheet: Color the surprise circle in each recipe and write the new color.

Butterfly Wing Painter Worksheet for Age 4

A butterfly with empty wings: color the sections, and try making both wings match like the Magic Mirror.

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The game’s Magic Mirror paints both wings the same; the sheet asks your child to be the mirror — matching each left-wing section with the same color on the right. Symmetry plus color naming in one calm activity.

  • Symmetry: matching left to right
  • Color naming and repeating a color on purpose
  • Coloring medium-sized regions
  • Checking work against the mirror line

On the sheet: Color the butterfly — can you make both wings match?

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The sundae studio is pure creative choice, and paper keeps it that way: color the scoops, draw toppings, name the flavor. Naming an invented flavor is early expressive language wearing an ice-cream costume.

  • Making and describing creative choices
  • Coloring scoops and toppings
  • Inventing and saying a flavor name
  • Enjoying the process without a “correct” answer

On the sheet: Color and decorate the sundae, then design your own in the empty bowls.

What your child practices.

  • Pencil control on curves

On the sheet: Paint the pot, then design two more pots any way you like.

What your child practices.

The weather machine builds a rainbow in order; the sheet asks your child to color seven numbered arcs in the same red-to-purple order. Number order plus color order in one job — say both aloud: “one red, two orange…”

  • Rainbow color order (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple)
  • Following numbered steps
  • Counting 1–7 while coloring
  • Careful arc coloring

On the sheet: Color the rainbow arcs in number order with the color list.

Crystal Cave Colors Worksheet for Age 4

Warm colors or cool colors? Sort the cave’s treasures into the right crystal jars.

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The cave game sorts warm from cool; the sheet does it with cut-and-glue cards. Sorting by color TEMPERATURE is a big-deal art idea made simple: things that feel like sunshine versus things that feel like water.

  • Sorting warm vs cool colors
  • Scissor and glue practice
  • Saying the rule: “warm like fire, cool like water”
  • Checking a sorted group

On the sheet: Cut the cards. Glue warm things in the warm jar, cool things in the cool jar.
